index_title: Finite symmetric CCO targets, automorphism 2-groups and uniform real algebraicity
scope: Private B042: FOUR selected new Foundations I results, twelve definitions, 50 human claims and eight tasks, with NO auxiliary equations. The existing actual-fibre inheritance lemma remains a precisely selected canonical_hull C09/C10 import, not duplicate coverage or a circular Hasse input. Derive atom bipartiteness using internal high-girth graphs; expand Cauchy, finite p-group normalizer/maximal-index and subgroup/equivalence correspondence locally. Obtain finite Aut(F) a 2-group, transitive finite Hasse covers of index two, power-of-two real fibre sizes and a uniform real acl bound. Symmetry is retained by both short corollaries. No SAP, arbitrary imaginary CCO, elementary-abelian conclusion or new external published theorem. An independent bipartition bit-code proves |F|<=2^(number of occurring diversity colours) without transitivity/homogeneity as internal support.
scope_explanation: statement and proof. Separate faithful actual Aut(F) from generic nonfaithful actions, arbitrary finite symmetric CCO targets from transitive/homogeneous specializations, and real one-point fibres from imaginaries. Use only the finite graph part of parity_hasse and C09/C10 of fibreCCO; no imported Hasse theorem.

assumptions.name: Finite symmetric complete atomic target
assumptions.statement: F is a FINITE one-sort complete atomic binary structure. Each ordered distinct pair has exactly one named irreflexive diversity atom and every atom is SYMMETRIC. Equality is logical, separate from diversity; unused relation names do not affect atom graphs. No transitivity, homogeneity, SAP or finite bound on unused names is assumed for bipartiteness or the automorphism 2-group theorem. The signature is this atomic colour code (plus constant sort/unary data), with no extra nonconstant unary predicates, functions or higher-arity relations.

assumptions.name: Finite-target semantic HOMOMORPHIC CCO
assumptions.statement: Every finite partial diversity diagram whose specified simple cycles admit colour-preserving homomorphisms into F has a homomorphism of the WHOLE diagram into F. Nonadjacent vertices may collide. In the monochromatic argument all specified edges have one symmetric irreflexive atom. No injective completion is assumed.

assumptions.name: Optional transitivity for finite Hasse/cardinality
assumptions.statement: For Hasse covers and power-of-two target cardinality, F is NONEMPTY and FULL Aut(F) is transitive on F. Empty F has no proper invariant-equivalence cover and is handled separately. This premise is NOT used for atom bipartiteness or Aut(F) being a 2-group.

assumptions.name: Optional finite-target homogeneity for colour/orbit recognition
assumptions.statement: For the source chain-to-palette bound, F is ultrahomogeneous in its complete atomic binary signature. Then two ordered distinct pairs of the same named colour are in one FULL Aut(F) orbit; diagonal is one orbit using A03. This premise is NOT used by bipartiteness, the 2-group theorem or Hasse index two. The independent bit-code palette bound does not need it either.

assumptions.name: Actual inhabited original real source and finite palette
assumptions.statement: M is an INHABITED transitive ultrahomogeneous original one-sort complete symmetric binary source with FINITE named diversity palette D, d=|D|, and semantic homomorphic CCO. A finite real base A is a complete induced subset; realized one-point qf types of points outside A are given by their spokes and inequalities. Real acl means full-Aut(M/A) finite orbits (equivalent to usual algebraicity via the definable realized qf orbit). No SAP or arbitrary imaginary inheritance is assumed; countability is not needed by these local arguments.

assumptions.name: Independent finite-group counting setting
assumptions.statement: K is an arbitrary FINITE group and p is prime. Cauchy is a CONDITIONAL conclusion when p divides |K|. Use explicit finite products, cyclic tuple rotation and coset/orbit counting; no Cauchy theorem is imported or assumed. The group can be noncommutative and need not act faithfully on an auxiliary set.

assumptions.name: Independent finite p-group subgroup setting
assumptions.statement: L is a finite group of order p^k for a prime p, and H<L is a proper subgroup. For the maximal-index conclusion H is additionally maximal proper. Orbit sizes are computed by elementary coset partitions; the normalizer condition and index-p theorem are proved locally, not imported.

assumptions.name: Independent transitive action for subgroup correspondence
assumptions.statement: G is ANY group acting transitively on a NONEMPTY finite set Omega, possibly NONFAITHFULLY. Fix x in Omega and consider actual G-invariant equivalences U,V. The subgroup/equivalence correspondence and relative index bijections are elementary action statements; the cover premise is used only conditionally for maximality. No CCO, symmetry, p-group or homogeneous structure is needed for this correspondence.

imports.name: Internal high-girth/high-chromatic graph
imports.statement: For positive q,g choose a finite simple H with girth>g and chromatic number>q. Select ONLY the internally proved finite graph export C05, with its probability/sparsening ancestry; no original Hasse/CCO or RAW exact theorem from that module is imported. Connectedness is unnecessary here; no new Erdos axiom.

imports.name: Actual real fibre orbit/homogeneity and HOM CCO only
imports.statement: Over a complete finite ACTUAL REAL base, each realized outside one-point fibre is its full pointwise-stabilizer orbit, nonempty transitive and induced homogeneous, and inherits semantic HOM CCO. Real orbit algebraicity agrees with usual algebraicity because this realized qf orbit is definable. Select C09/C10 ONLY: neither C03 triangle fullness nor canonical_hull Hasse imports are used, avoiding a circular Hasse dependency.

definitions.name: Actual undirected atom graph
definitions.statement: For each named diversity atom a use the finite simple graph with vertices F and edges {x,y} where a(x,y). Symmetry makes it undirected; irreflexivity forbids loops. An unused atom gives an edgeless graph.

definitions.name: Cycle homomorphism as a closed atom walk
definitions.statement: A colour-preserving map from a formal m-cycle to the a-graph is a closed a-walk of length m; repeated target vertices/backtracking are allowed. A simple odd target cycle has odd length r>=3.

definitions.name: High-girth obstruction request
definitions.statement: Given an odd a-cycle of length r, take q=|F| and g=r in I01. Its existence implies |F|>=r>=3, discharging positivity. Colour EVERY H edge a without requiring other pair colours in the partial input.

definitions.name: Cyclic p-tuples with product identity
definitions.statement: T_p(K)={(g1,...,gp):g1...gp=1}. The last entry is determined by the first p-1, so |T_p(K)|=|K|^(p-1). Rotate coordinates cyclically; product-one is preserved by conjugation even in nonabelian K.

definitions.name: Normalizer and finite p-group maximality
definitions.statement: N_L(H)={g:g^-1 H g=H}; H acts by left multiplication on left cosets L/H. Fixed cosets correspond exactly to N_L(H)/H. Prove proper H<N_L(H) by orbit counting before invoking maximality.

definitions.name: Base stabilizer interval
definitions.statement: For actual invariant U on Omega put H_U={g:gx U x}, containing G_x. Conversely for G_x<=H<=G, identify Omega with G/G_x and take the kernel of G/G_x->G/H. No normality or faithfulness is required.

definitions.name: Relative cover index and saturated chain
definitions.statement: [V:U] counts U-classes inside one V-class, uniform in a transitive action. A Hasse cover is a strict inclusion of invariant equivalences with nothing between. A saturated finite chain from Id to top includes only Hasse covers; singleton carrier has a zero-step chain.

definitions.name: Occurring finite target diversity palette
definitions.statement: D_F is the finite set of actually occurring diversity colours in F, with d_F=|D_F|. It is finite because F has finitely many ordered pairs, even if the signature has unused names. Identifying each colour with one full pair orbital is a further homogeneous conclusion C31.

definitions.name: Actual outside-real one-point fibre
definitions.statement: For finite A subset M and realized q(x/A) of x outside A, X_q is exactly the points having the prescribed diversity spokes to every anchor and all inequalities x!=a. It is an ACTUAL real subset, not an arbitrary quotient/tuple imaginary.

definitions.name: Real finite-orbit algebraicity
definitions.statement: acl_M(A) is the set of real points with finite full-Aut(M/A) orbit. Every anchor is fixed. I02 identifies outside orbits with definable realized qf fibres, so this agrees with usual real model-theoretic algebraicity.

definitions.name: One-point spoke vector over nonempty real A
definitions.statement: Fix an enumeration of |A|=n>=1 anchors. Every outside point gives one vector in D^n; complete original binarity makes this vector determine its entire one-point qf type over the fixed base. No equality spoke occurs, and no 0^0 convention is used.

definitions.name: Independent bipartition bit code
definitions.statement: Choose an arbitrary proper 2-colouring c_a of each occurring atom graph, with no invariance/canonicality requirement. Code x by (c_a(x))_(a in D_F). Different components can be flipped independently; completeness will force distinct vertices to have distinct bit codes.

claims.name: An odd atom cycle is the only obstruction to bipartiteness
claims.statement: Fix a diversity atom a. If its simple undirected graph is not bipartite, a breadth-first parity colouring conflict supplies a simple odd a-cycle of length r>=3. Thus F has at least r points. Empty/singleton targets and unused atoms have no such obstruction.

claims.name: Choose an H of girth greater than r and chromatic number greater than F
claims.statement: In the C01 contradiction case use I01 with q=|F|>=3 and g=r>=3. Obtain finite simple H, girth(H)>r and chi(H)>|F|. Regard its edges as a partial monochromatic a-diagram; unspecified pairs impose no relation.

claims.name: Every even specified H-cycle folds onto one a-edge
claims.statement: A simple even m-cycle maps alternately to the two endpoints of an a-edge from the given odd target cycle. Every edge, including closure, is a-coloured; reverse traversal uses SYMMETRY. This is a homomorphism, with arbitrary repeated target vertices.

claims.name: Every odd H-cycle maps to the given odd cycle with backtracks
claims.statement: For odd length m, girth(H)>r gives m>r and m-r is a nonnegative even integer. Traverse the fixed r-cycle and add (m-r)/2 two-edge backtracking excursions along one of its a-edges. The resulting closed a-walk has exactly length m, hence is a homomorphism of that m-cycle. Symmetry is essential for each reverse step.

claims.name: All specified H simple cycles are homomorphically feasible
claims.statement: C03 handles all even cycle lengths and C04 all odd lengths. Different cycles may use different maps and collisions. No whole H map, finite-target CCO, homogeneity, transitivity or SAP has yet been invoked.

claims.name: HOM CCO would yield an impossible proper F-colouring of H
claims.statement: Apply A02 to the C02 partial a-diagram using C05 cycle feasibility, obtaining h:H->F preserving every a-edge. Irreflexivity forces distinct images on adjacent vertices, so h is a proper vertex colouring with at most |F| colours. This contradicts chi(H)>|F|.

claims.name: Every finite symmetric CCO atom graph is bipartite
claims.statement: C01-C06 exclude every odd cycle, hence every a-graph is bipartite. This proves lem:bip, including empty/singleton F, edgeless/unused atoms and disconnected graphs. It needs neither transitivity, homogeneity nor SAP, and introduces no new external Erdos input.

claims.name: A bipartition bit code bounds F by 2 to the occurring palette size
claims.statement: Choose the finite family of bipartitions supplied by C07 and form D12. For x!=y, completeness gives their occurring colour a; the edge forces c_a(x)!=c_a(y), so their bit codes differ. The code is injective into {0,1}^(D_F), giving |F|<=2^d_F, WITHOUT transitivity or homogeneity. Empty D_F allows at most one point. This is internal stronger support, not another numbered source export.

claims.name: Product-one p-tuples have the explicit finite count
claims.statement: For finite K and prime p, p>=2. Choosing the first p-1 entries of D04 arbitrarily uniquely determines the last as their inverse product, so |T_p(K)|=|K|^(p-1). If p divides |K| this count is divisible by p.

claims.name: Cyclic rotation gives the Cauchy fixed-point congruence
claims.statement: Rotation preserves product-one because g2...gp g1=g1^-1(g1...gp)g1. Its orbits have size one or p: a nontrivial period modulo prime p generates all rotations. Fixed tuples are exactly (g,...,g) with g^p=1. Therefore their number is congruent to |T_p(K)| modulo p. This works for noncommutative K.

claims.name: Local Cauchy proof produces an element of order p
claims.statement: CONDITIONAL on p dividing |K|, C09/C10 make the number of fixed tuples divisible by p. It is positive because the identity tuple is fixed, hence at least p. A second fixed tuple gives nonidentity g with g^p=1; primeness makes its order exactly p. This proves the needed Cauchy support internally.

claims.name: A positive finite group order not a power of two has an odd prime divisor
claims.statement: Repeatedly factor 2 out of |K|>=1. If the remaining odd integer is greater than one, its least divisor greater than one is an odd prime; otherwise |K| is 2^k. The trivial group has order 2^0. This elementary integer reduction is independent of CCO or actions.

claims.name: A nontrivial order-p AUTOMORPHISM has a moved p-orbit
claims.statement: Aut(F) is a finite subgroup of the permutation group of F. If an odd prime p divides its order, C11 supplies sigma of order p. As an ACTUAL nonidentity permutation it moves some x. The cyclic orbit length divides p and is not one, so x,sigma x,...,sigma^(p-1)x are p distinct points. This moved-point step uses the faithfulness of actual Aut(F), not of generic later actions.

claims.name: That p-orbit is a monochromatic simple odd cycle
claims.statement: Let a=col(x,sigma x), a diversity atom by C13. Applying powers of sigma preserves that same colour on every consecutive pair, INCLUDING the closing pair sigma^(p-1)x,x. Symmetry makes this an undirected a-cycle of odd length p>=3. No transitivity/homogeneity of F is required.

claims.name: The full finite automorphism group has power-of-two order
claims.statement: C14 contradicts C07 bipartiteness if any odd prime divides |Aut(F)|. C12 therefore gives |Aut(F)|=2^k, including empty/singleton F and trivial group k=0. This proves cor:twogroup in its inherited SYMMETRIC complete-atomic CCO setting, not for arbitrary directed colours.

claims.name: A subgroup acting on p-group cosets has p-power orbit sizes
claims.statement: For H<L in A07, coset partition counting gives |H| and [L:H] powers of p. An H-orbit on L/H is in bijection with H/Stab_H(c), so every orbit size is a p-power; each nonfixed orbit has size divisible by p. Since H is proper, |L/H| is divisible by p.

claims.name: Fixed cosets are exactly normalizer cosets
claims.statement: A left coset gH is fixed by all H iff g^-1 H g is contained in H. Both finite subgroups have the same size, so containment is equality; equivalently g lies in N_L(H). Thus the fixed-coset count is [N_L(H):H], and the coset H is always fixed.

claims.name: The finite p-group normalizer condition follows by counting
claims.statement: Total coset count is divisible by p and all nonfixed orbit sizes are divisible by p by C16. Therefore the positive fixed-coset count C17 is divisible by p, hence >=p. Thus H<N_L(H). No assumption that H is normal was made.

claims.name: A maximal proper subgroup of a finite p-group is normal
claims.statement: IF H is maximal proper, C18 gives H<N_L(H)<=L, so maximality forces N_L(H)=L. Hence H is normal in L and L/H is a nontrivial finite p-group.

claims.name: A maximal proper finite p-group subgroup has index p
claims.statement: If the C19 quotient had order p^k with k>1, C11 applied to it supplies an order-p subgroup, nontrivial and proper. Its inverse image would be a subgroup strictly between H and L, contradicting maximality. Thus |L/H|=p and [L:H]=p, in particular index two for p=2.

claims.name: An invariant equivalence gives a subgroup above the point stabilizer
claims.statement: For invariant U, H_U={g:gx U x} contains G_x and identity. If g,h lie in it, invariance sends hx U x to ghx U gx, and transitivity of U gives ghx U x. Invariance/symmetry similarly gives g^-1 x U x. Thus H_U is a subgroup.

claims.name: Coset kernels give the inverse invariant-equivalence correspondence
claims.statement: Transitivity identifies Omega with G/G_x by gG_x->gx. For any G_x<=H<=G the projection to G/H is well-defined/equivariant; its kernel is a G-invariant equivalence. Its base subgroup is exactly H. Conversely an invariant U is recovered from H_U by translating arbitrary pairs to x. Therefore this is an inclusion-preserving bijection, with no faithfulness/normality assumption.

claims.name: Relative class counts equal subgroup indices uniformly
claims.statement: For U<=V, the map hH_U -> the U-class of hx bijects H_V/H_U with U-classes inside V(x). Well-definedness/injectivity follow by translating U, and surjectivity by G-transitivity. Hence [V:U]=[H_V:H_U]. Translating V(x) to any other V-class gives the same number, even for a nonfaithful action.

claims.name: An invariant Hasse cover makes the two subgroups a maximal pair
claims.statement: CONDITIONAL on U<V being a Hasse cover, any H_U<L<H_V contains G_x. C22 would give an invariant equivalence strictly between U and V. Therefore no such L exists and H_U is maximal proper in H_V. This is a pure transitive-action fact, independent of CCO or p-groups.

claims.name: Apply the correspondence to the ACTUAL transitive finite target
claims.statement: Under A03 use G=FULL Aut(F) and a point x in F. C15 makes G a finite 2-group; its subgroup H_V also has 2-power order by finite coset counting. For any invariant cover U<V, C21-C24 provide subgroups H_U maximal proper in H_V. No exactness or original relative Hasse provider is imported.

claims.name: The maximal-subgroup index is exactly the relative Hasse index
claims.statement: Use C20 at p=2 for H_U<H_V from C25, obtaining [H_V:H_U]=2. C23 identifies it with the number of U-classes in EVERY V-class. Thus [V:U]=2.

claims.name: Finite transitive symmetric CCO Hasse-cover source export
claims.statement: C26 proves cor:hasse for ALL invariant-equivalence covers, without any exactness restriction. Transitivity is used for uniformity/correspondence; neither homogeneity nor SAP is needed for this finite result. The scope is finite symmetric CCO targets, not an AP-only or arbitrary imaginary Hasse theorem.

claims.name: Small targets do not require contradictory graph/group requests
claims.statement: Empty/singleton F has no odd atom cycle, Aut(F) is trivial, and no proper invariant-equivalence cover exists. Hasse proofs choose x only under the nonempty A03 premise; an empty case has a vacuous cover assertion. The later empty-base cardinality statement retains INHABITED original M, so it never claims zero is a power of two.

claims.name: Actual real fibres are exactly definable full-stabilizer orbits
claims.statement: For finite real A and x outside A, I02 identifies X_q with Aut(M/A).x. The realized qf type is the finite conjunction of spoke atoms and inequalities, hence its fibre is definable. It is finite iff x is real algebraic over A; anchors themselves are fixed. This is not a statement about hidden/tuple coordinates.

claims.name: Every finite actual fibre has precisely the required finite CCO structure
claims.statement: By I02 each realized X_q is nonempty, transitive, induced homogeneous and inherits semantic HOM CCO. If finite, its induced actual palette is symmetric complete atomic, containing at most the d original diversity colours. Only canonical_hull C09/C10 are used, not C03 triangle fullness or any imported Hasse claim.

claims.name: Homogeneous target pair orbitals are its occurring named colours
claims.statement: In a transitive homogeneous finite F, the diagonal is one orbit. Two ordered distinct pairs with the same named atom define an induced two-point isomorphism (symmetry/converses and constant unary data agree), which homogeneity extends. Thus each occurring named diversity colour is ONE full Aut(F) pair orbital; different colours cannot merge. This requires no CCO.

claims.name: Choose a finite saturated chain of all invariant equivalences
claims.statement: For finite nonempty transitive F the invariant-equivalence lattice is finite, contains Id and top, and therefore has a saturated finite chain Id=U0<...<Um=top. For one point take m=0. Relative block counts telescope from singleton size to |F| under transitivity. No homogeneity or CCO is used in choosing the chain.

claims.name: Index-two covers make target cardinality a power of two
claims.statement: Under finite transitive symmetric HOM CCO, apply C27 to every step of C32. Each relative index is two, so telescoping gives |F|=2^m, including m=0 for a singleton. Homogeneity is NOT needed for this power-of-two conclusion.

claims.name: Each strict homogeneous chain step consumes a new occurring colour
claims.statement: In the C32 chain, each difference U_(i+1) minus U_i contains a distinct pair because every equivalence contains equality. By C31 both relations are unions of full named colour orbitals, so an entire previously absent diversity colour is added. The differences are disjoint for different steps, giving m<=d_F. For an actual fibre d_F<=d. The inequality m<=d_F itself uses no CCO; CCO enters the separate index-two cover-size step C33.

claims.name: Finite homogeneous transitive target size is 2^m with m<=its palette
claims.statement: Combine C33 and C34: |F|=2^m with 0<=m<=d_F. This generic local support can be instantiated at finite actual fibres or at finite original M; it is not another counted source result.

claims.name: There are at most d^n outside real one-point types over A
claims.statement: For n=|A|>=1, list its anchors. Completeness, original binarity and one-sort transitivity make each outside qf type determined by its n diversity-spoke colours, an element of D^n. Thus there are at most d^n realized outside types, independently of which vectors are actually consistent. No equal-to-anchor type is included.

claims.name: Real acl is the anchors plus the disjoint finite actual fibres
claims.statement: C29 partitions M minus A into its actual realized one-point orbits. A point outside A is algebraic iff its fibre is finite. Hence acl_M(A)=A union the disjoint union of finite X_q. C30/C35 give each such finite nonempty fibre cardinal 2^m with m<=d_F<=d.

claims.name: Summing fibre sizes proves the uniform real closure bound
claims.statement: There are at most d^n finite fibres by C36, each has size at most 2^d by C37, and anchors contribute n. Thus |acl_M(A)|<=n+d^n 2^d for n>=1. In particular acl is locally finite with a bound depending only on base size and the finite original diversity palette, not on a chosen realization.

claims.name: For an empty base in infinite transitive M there is no real algebraicity
claims.statement: Under A05, full Aut(M) has the single orbit M. If M is infinite this orbit is infinite, so acl_M(empty)=empty. This argument uses only transitivity and infinitude, not fibre inheritance, finite Hasse, bipartiteness, group counting or SAP.

claims.name: For an empty base in finite inhabited M the same chain gives a bounded power of two
claims.statement: If original M is finite, it satisfies the finite transitive homogeneous symmetric HOM CCO support hypotheses itself. Apply C35 to F=M, with d_F<=d: acl_M(empty)=M has size 2^m for 0<=m<=d and hence at most 2^d. Inhabitedness rules out an empty cardinal being called a power of two.

claims.name: Uniform real algebraic-closure source export
claims.statement: C30/C35/C37 give every finite realized outside fibre size 2^m with 0<=m<=d. C38 gives n+d^n 2^d for nonempty real bases, while C39/C40 give the distinct empty-base cases. This proves cor:fibre-uniform-acl on ACTUAL real points only, without SAP or arbitrary imaginary CCO inheritance.

claims.name: The zero-palette and singleton conventions require no 0^0
claims.statement: If d=0, completeness forces inhabited original M to have one point. For a nonempty real base the outside type set is empty and d^n=0 with n>=1, so C38 reduces to the anchor bound. Empty bases are handled by C39/C40, never by evaluating a d^0 type-count formula. Finite realized fibres are always inhabited.

claims.name: The bit-code route independently bounds the power-of-two exponent
claims.statement: C08 gives |F|<=2^d_F for ANY finite symmetric CCO target. If also transitive, C33 gives |F|=2^m, and strict monotonicity of natural powers of two yields m<=d_F. Thus this alternate bound does NOT require homogeneity/colour-orbit recognition, although C34 explicitly expands the source chain proof as well. It is internal support, not a new numbered export.

claims.name: Symmetry is essential: directed mod-three difference colours are outside scope
claims.statement: On Z/3 name the two oriented diversity colours y-x=+1 and -1. A partial colour diagram is a mod-three potential system; if every specified simple cycle is feasible, all cycle sums vanish and potentials yield a homomorphism, so semantic HOM CCO holds. Its full automorphism group is translations C3, not a 2-group. This lies OUTSIDE the symmetric A01 premise, which both short source corollaries retain.

claims.name: Without transitivity relative cover counts need not be uniform
claims.statement: For C2 acting by swapping 0,1 and fixing 2, Id is covered by the invariant equivalence with blocks {0,1},{2}. Local relative class counts are 2 and 1, so no common index two exists. This is a generic ACTION boundary, not a claim of a finite symmetric HOM CCO source; regular C3 has a cover of index three only outside the 2-group hypotheses.

claims.name: A finite 2-group conclusion is not an elementary-abelian or regular-action claim
claims.statement: C15/C27 prove power-of-two automorphism order and invariant cover index two. They assert neither abelianness, exponent two, regularity, SAP, arbitrary quotient inheritance nor intrinsic owner-kernel binding. Generic p-group support permits nonabelian groups such as D8/Q8 and nonfaithful auxiliary actions.

claims.name: The complete one-colour triangle is not HOM CCO
claims.statement: K3 has a nonbipartite diversity atom graph, so C07 shows it cannot have semantic HOM CCO. Concretely the finite triangle-free 4-chromatic Mycielski(C5) graph has every simple cycle K3-homomorphic (even folds and odd lengths>=5) but no whole K3 homomorphism. This also guards against replacing CCO by finite completeness/AP alone.

claims.name: Actual real fibres are not arbitrary imaginary or owner-kernel sorts
claims.statement: I02 is restricted to realized real one-point fibres over an actual complete real base. C41 therefore bounds REAL acl and does not assert CCO for arbitrary nonexact quotient/tuple imaginaries or describe a hidden pointwise owner-kernel action. Additional exact-quotient or encoding theorems would be separate inputs.

claims.name: The type count depends on complete original binarity and the finite palette
claims.statement: C36 counts realized ONE-point real qf types by n spokes in one original transitive binary sort. It is not a bound for arbitrary higher-arity signatures, extra function closures, hidden parameters or tuple types. The bound depends on n, and no uniform constant independent of base size is asserted.

claims.name: An infinite palette can have infinite real acl despite symmetric HOM CCO
claims.statement: Let M be the direct sum of countably many F2 coordinates, naming EVERY nonzero difference g as R_g(x,y) iff y=x+g. All atoms are symmetric; the countable source is transitive and homogeneous because any nonempty partial isomorphism is a translation. Partial edge constraints are difference equations, solvable iff all simple cycle sums vanish, so HOM CCO holds. But every point is uniquely definable over one real anchor by its named difference relation, so acl({a})=M is infinite. This is OUTSIDE A05 finite-palette scope.

overview_notes: There are no new external published inputs: high-girth graphs were already proved internally, and Cauchy/maximal-index support is expanded here.
Symmetry is retained by both short source corollaries; directed mod-three colours give a boundary example.
The actual fibre import selects C09/C10 only; no earlier Hasse/triangle-fullness claim is smuggled into the finite proof.
Full-Aut fibre pair orbitals equal occurring named colours; this justifies the source chain-to-palette count.
The independent bipartition bit code gives the same palette bound with fewer hypotheses; it is internal support, not another numbered source result.
The result concerns actual real acl; arbitrary imaginaries and infinite palettes remain outside the conclusion.
